name: Deterministic 16-bit Animation Assembly Engine
purpose: Translate the semantic animation director's scene directions into deterministic, frame-by-frame pixel placement without changing source art assets.

scope.rawArtPolicy: Do not generate, redesign, recolor, or modify source character art during assembly.
scope.legacyPolicy: Reject missing, legacy, or mismatched engine and layout references as unhandled errors.

anchorContract.shadowRule: contact_shadow_anchor stays bound to the rendered feet position and follows scale changes

executionGraph: Resolve the requested walk band and its baseline, scale, and horizontal limits.
Resolve the named near anchor and use it as the destination intent.
Place the frame from its feet anchor, then derive orientation and integer-pixel motion.
Sort actors by feet_y and apply declared foreground occlusion after actor layers.

layers.background: Walls, machines, doors, and static set dressing.
layers.midground: The playable actor walk bands and contact shadows.
layers.foreground: Declared occluders such as conveyor faces, desk fronts, and crates.

walkBands.rear: Upper floor edge, smallest approved scale.
walkBands.front: Lower floor edge, largest approved scale.

depthSorting.order: Lower feet_y draws behind greater feet_y.
depthSorting.occlusion: A foreground occluder wins whenever its declared mask covers an actor with a lower depth priority.

validationCriteria.rule: Reject a feet anchor above the active walk-band baseline.
Reject a feet anchor below the legal floor boundary.
Reject a depth assignment that conflicts with the set's vertical layout.
Reject movement steps that are not aligned to the authored walk-cycle timing.
Reject a contact shadow detached from the feet tracking point.
Reject an actor drawn over a foreground mask when the actor should be behind it.
Every non-idle state names the line, reaction, prop, or transition it serves.
Every state has bounded start/end times and links to its previous/next state.
Rendered visible alpha bounds never overlap another actor in the same frame.
Animation direction cannot alter approved title, premise, beats, dialogue, bark events, TV interruptions, music, or continuity.
Every human line names a distinct listener, intent, reaction opportunity, and post-line reaction.
Every visible prop is tied to a locked line by an explicit dialogue keyword and recorded purpose.
The hook establishes the scene, conflict uses readable two/group shots, reversals show reactions, and the final button holds.
Walking, entering, and exiting require a line, reaction, prop, entrance, exit, or transition purpose.
Every fallback or missing authored action is listed in motion.assetNeeds and is never hidden.

agentBrief: Use semantic locations, named anchors, and walk bands; never invent arbitrary world coordinates.
Use feet anchors rather than canvas centers, heads, or transparent margins for all placement.
Keep all translation, scale, and sorting values on the integer pixel grid.
Use authored idle, talk, reaction, bark, and walk clips; do not make the dashboard or live character grid walk by default.
Keep Bork bark-only and preserve the supplied character identity and silhouette.
Reject the frame and report the exact validation failure instead of silently compensating.

actionRegistry.resolution: requested clip_action resolves through the per-character CHARACTER-CATALOG actionRegistry; missing exact clips use a recorded verified fallback
actionRegistry.fallbackPolicy: missing or unverified clips are never silently replaced without fallback metadata

stateMachine.defaultState: grounded idle when no higher-priority timed cue is active
stateMachine.transitionPolicy: talk and bark are locked to measured audio; react/listen states are anchored to the line they serve; walk/enter/exit require a semantic travel cue
stateMachine.timing: all times are relative to the content segment; the final media tail is measured from the last audible word with a 30 ms pad

shots.rule: shots support readability and purpose; they do not move actors outside the deterministic layout solver

collisionPolicy.check: every rendered frame, including moving frames
collisionPolicy.response: reroute a legal actor path or quarantine the segment with measured collision pairs
